newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil prisoners free one hostage, seige continues.
newsitem.headline: Brazil prisoners free one hostage, seige continues.

text.p: A group of about 15 Brazilian prisoners released a hostage in a rebellion that has lasted nearly a week and shows no sign of ending, local Globo television said on Friday.

The rebels, whose escape bid was foiled six days ago, were demanding cars, arms and cash in a bid to leave the prison in Vitoria da Conquista, Bahia state. Police have said they will not supply any guns or ammunition.
Negotiators on Friday offered to free three of the rebellious prisoners and transfer the others to jails near their families but the offer was rejected.
Police have been trying to wear the prisoners down by blaring sirens and staging explosions throughout the night outside the occupied area.
"An invasion ... will only happen if there is an attack on the lives of the hostages," police officer Waldir Barbosa told Globo.
The seven remaining hostages have made several emotional pleas for police to resolve the situation.
"Every minute seems like a year for us," one hostage said.
Food and other necessities were being lowered over the walls into the exercise area using ropes, police said.
A police official said the rebellious prisoners seized their hostages during visiting hours on Saturday after an escape tunnel they had dug was discovered.
